A1.justification: The PDFs describe the same work, renamed from DPJL to VP-CMJL, with matching core components and retained results. Both ten-page PDFs are readable and end with references. However, v2 repeatedly cites an appendix and supplementary material containing settings and analyses that are absent from the supplied PDF, limiting those comparisons.

before.justification: v1 reports original CZSL benchmark results, component and decomposition ablations, and qualitative predictions in Section 4.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds closed-world VAW-CZSL results in Table 2.

M1.justification: v2 replaces explicit unweighted loss sums with weighted branch losses and supervised/KL balancing terms in Equations 9, 17 and 19. The CLIP/adapter architecture, CA/MLP decomposition, text-initialized visual centers and KL alignment remain. Renaming DPJL to VP-CMJL does not establish a new architecture, and the default inference fusion is equivalent up to scaling.

E1.justification: v2 adds closed-world evaluation on VAW-CZSL's real-world attribute-object compositions. MIT-States, UT-Zappos and C-GQA remain, with their original closed/open-world coverage. This extends dataset coverage within the same CZSL task; no VAW-CZSL open-world results are supplied.

E2.justification: The original benchmark comparisons retain the same comparator membership. The added VAW-CZSL table compares against CLIP, CSP, DFSP and the newly reported CAILA comparator. CAILA's citation [18] points to the DFSP paper in v2's references, leaving its attribution inconsistent.

E3.justification: The stated metrics, closed/open-world definitions and 20-epoch budget remain unchanged. However, v2 omits the earlier split and optimization specifications and refers to unavailable supplementary material. The detailed VAW-CZSL protocol and whether settings behind retained results changed cannot be reliably established.

E4.justification: Tables 3–4 and Figure 4 retain the component-removal ablations, decomposition-module comparisons and qualitative cases. v2 adds Figure 5's feature-space comparison but does not identify its data or construction procedure. It also claims initialization and hyperparameter analyses in an absent supplement, preventing verification of their empirical basis and extent.

E5.justification: Neither supplied PDF reports repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, standard deviations or significance tests. The benchmark and ablation tables continue to report point estimates.

E6.justification: All numerical entries in v1 Table 2 match v2 Table 1, and Tables 3–4 retain their values. v2 adds VAW-CZSL results: VP-CMJL reports S/U/HM/AUC of 47.8/51.1/38.2/20.7, versus CAILA's 41.6/49.2/34.6/17.2. These are additional benchmark results, not gains over the earlier version under an established identical setting.

T1.justification: v2 Equation 15 uses each visual branch's corresponding decomposed feature, correcting the inconsistency in v1 Equations 20–21, which use the composition feature despite the stated MLP decomposition. The formal loss definitions also gain weighting coefficients. The class-center decomposition and orthogonality argument are retained, with no added theorem or proof.

C1.justification: v2 extends the benchmark claim from three datasets to four. Its conclusion also replaces v1's qualified claim of competitive open-world performance with a broader state-of-the-art claim covering both settings. The retained MIT-States results still place VP-CMJL below CDS-CZSL on open-world HM and AUC.

C2.justification: v2 adds an explanation linking random initialization to sparse training signals and suboptimal local optima, and interprets Figure 5 through bidirectional cross-modal adjustment. It condenses v1's discussion of hierarchical label ambiguity on MIT-States into a shorter explanation emphasizing CDS-CZSL's pruning and the proposed method's avoidance of such task-specific optimization.

D1.justification: v1 supplies dataset split counts, Adam, the StepLR decay schedule, dataset-specific learning rates and weight decay. These details are unavailable in the supplied v2, which points to missing supplementary material and does not specify its new loss-weight values. v2 newly documents the 'a photo of' prompt initialization, specifies ViT-L/14, and reports A800 instead of A6000 GPUs.

R1.justification: The Prototype Learning discussion becomes Visual Center Learning, positioning novelty around textual guidance of visual centers and expanding criticism of visual-only prototypes. Five references disappear, including Snell et al.'s prototypical networks and Jing et al.'s retrieval-augmented primitive representations. Most CZSL and VLM positioning remains.

P1.justification: The title, method terminology, abstract, introduction and conclusion are extensively rewritten. Section 3 is reorganized around Basic Framework, nested Text-Guided Visual Proxy Learning, and Cross-Modal Joint Learning; repeated branch equations are consolidated. These changes substantially revise the narrative despite retaining much of the underlying method.

P2.justification: v2 revises the motivating illustration and framework annotations, adds Figure 5 and the VAW-CZSL table, and omits the dataset-statistics table from the supplied document. Existing tables are resized or relocated, and Figure 3 moves within the method section. The two-column format and most existing displays, including Figure 4's cases, remain recognizable.

improvement.justification: The additional VAW-CZSL results and reorganized explanation provide useful gains. However, essential optimization details, new loss-weight settings and claimed supplementary analyses are unavailable, while the CAILA citation and broader open-world conclusion weaken the ability to check comparisons and claims. These unresolved documentation gaps prevent a reliable net quality judgment despite the added empirical coverage.
